name: Catalina Crunch Protein Cereal — Chocolate Peanut Butter

source.author: Catalina Crunch
source.notes: Requested via iHerb (il.iherb.com), egress-blocked by the proxy — values from Catalina Crunch's published label via web (manufacturer/retailer). 9 oz (255 g) bag ≈ 7 servings. Total-carb / net-carb split is approximate (sweetened with stevia + monk fruit, no sugar alcohols). Plant-based (pea-protein) cereal. Contains peanuts; processed with milk + tree nuts.

serving_desc: 1 serving (½ cup, ~36 g) — 9 oz (255 g) bag ≈ 7 servings

ingredients.item: Catalina flour (pea protein, corn flour, tapioca starch, corn/pea/chicory/potato fiber, guar gum)
high-oleic sunflower oil, peanut oil, peanuts
leavening (monocalcium phosphate, baking soda, calcium carbonate)
natural flavors, stevia extract, monk fruit extract

steps: Eat as-is: with milk or Greek/PRO yogurt (adds protein and completes the pea protein), or dry as a snack / yogurt topping.

him.verdict: An excellent macro cereal — 11 g protein AND 9 g fiber for just 110 kcal, with 0 g sugar and ~7 g net carb. Same protein+fiber role as the Quest bar, but as a cereal: pour milk or Greek/PRO yogurt over it and you push protein higher AND complete the amino profile (the base is plant pea protein, slightly lower in methionine on its own). Great low-cal, high-satiety breakfast/snack. Knocks: ultra-processed, moderate sodium (~190 mg), pea protein less complete than dairy solo.
flags: 11 g protein + 9 g fiber for 110 kcal
plant (pea) protein — pair with dairy to complete it
suggested_mods: Eat with PRO yogurt or milk — adds protein and completes the amino profile
Great as a low-cal high-fiber breakfast on a cut, or a crunchy yogurt topping
Watch total servings — it's easy to pour more than one ½-cup serving

her_preconception.verdict: A good high-protein, high-fiber option for her — 11 g protein and 9 g fiber (fiber helps pregnancy constipation), 0 sugar, plus a little plant iron. Stevia and monk fruit are non-nutritive sweeteners generally regarded as safe in pregnancy. Not a big prenatal micronutrient source. Contains peanuts (and made in a facility with milk/tree nuts) — note if relevant.
prenatal_highlights: 11 g protein + 9 g fiber per serving
a little plant iron (pair with a vitamin-C fruit to absorb it)

safety_advisories.note: Sweetened with stevia + monk fruit — non-nutritive sweeteners, considered safe in pregnancy in normal amounts; moderate if she prefers to limit them.
safety_advisories.swap: plain oats/whole-grain cereal if avoiding sweeteners

suggested_mods: Have it with PRO yogurt + berries for a balanced, prenatally-useful breakfast (protein + fiber + vitamin C)
Allergen: peanuts (facility also handles milk + tree nuts)
